title: Orbital AI Computing: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Satellite Scale
abstract: arXiv:2608.14557v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) computing is emerging for low-latency, globally distributed AI services, enabled by advances in satellite constellations and reusable launch systems. However, its sustainability remains unclear. Prior work introduces ESpaS, a framework for estimating lifecycle carbon intensity, but models systems using generic datacenter configurations and does not capture modern AI hardware, where power, mass, and compute characteristics vary widely and launch emissions scale with system mass. In this work, we extend ESpaS with accelerator-aware modeling and evaluate two representative systems: a lightweight Jetson AGX Orin for small satellites and a high-performance DGX H100 enabled by large-payload launch platforms. We show that launch emissions act as a fixed carbon overhead: low-mass systems minimize absolute emissions, while high-performance systems amortize this cost more effectively, reducing carbon intensity. translated_title: 轨道AI计算：卫星尺度上的碳权衡
translated_abstract: 低地球轨道（LEO）计算正因卫星星座和可重复使用发射系统的进步而兴起，用于提供低延迟、全球分布的AI服务。然而，其可持续性仍不明确。先前的研究提出了ESpaS框架，用于估算生命周期碳强度，但该框架使用通用数据中心配置建模系统，未能捕捉现代AI硬件的特点，其中功率、质量和计算特性差异显著，且发射排放随系统质量变化。在本研究中，我们扩展了ESpaS，加入加速器感知建模，并评估了两个代表性系统：用于小型卫星的轻量级Jetson AGX Orin和由大载荷发射平台支持的高性能DGX H100。我们表明，发射排放作为固定的碳开销：低质量系统最小化绝对排放，而高性能系统更有效地摊销这一成本，降低碳强度。因此，在轨道AI计算中，存在规模与碳效率之间的权衡。
tldr: 本研究扩展了ESpaS框架，引入加速器感知建模，揭示轨道AI计算中发射排放作为固定碳开销，低质量系统最小化绝对排放，而高性能系统通过更有效摊销成本降低碳强度，突出了卫星规模与碳效率之间的权衡。
en_tdlr: This work extends the ESpaS framework with accelerator-aware modeling, revealing that launch emissions act as a fixed carbon overhead in orbital AI computing, where low-mass systems minimize absolute emissions while high-performance systems reduce carbon intensity through better cost amortization, highlighting a tradeoff between satellite scale and carbon efficiency.
